name: Lysanias
overview: Lysanias was a male ruler known as the tetrarch of Abilene, a region referenced in the Gospel of Luke. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes in Scripture. His role as tetrarch identifies him as a local governor during the time of John the Baptist's ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Lysanias' is a proper name mentioned in Luke 3:1 without an explicit meaning given. His title, 'Tetrarch of Abilene,' signifies his political authority over the territory of Abilene, described as 'great prince of abiyliyn,' indicating his status as a regional ruler.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Lysanias beyond his designation as tetrarch of Abilene. No other relational information is provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Lysanias is significant in the biblical narrative as a historical marker situating the ministry of John the Baptist in a specific political and temporal context. His mention underscores the fulfillment of God's timing and sovereign orchestration in the unfolding of redemptive history. As tetrarch of Abilene, his governance helps frame the setting of Luke's Gospel during the early first century.
